task.title: Persist explicit provider-tool task continuations
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/569 by persisting one explicit continuation in its originating durable task and session while preserving caller-controlled progression and metadata-only tool evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight the active originating task, immutable session association, exact continuation transcript, unused Attempt identity, and fresh invocation identity before the provider call.
Call the owned continuation provider once, then persist final assistant content and Attempt or dispatch one subsequent tool request and return another exact in-memory continuation.
Reject stale transcripts before dispatch and guard final append atomically against a racing transcript change.
Preserve typed ordered failures, exact in-memory tool values, and metadata-only durable invocation evidence without retry, rollback, or an automatic next step.

attempts.summary: Established RED for durable final and chained-tool continuations.
attempts.diagnostic: ToolAssistantRuntime lacked a task bound continuation operation and the session store lacked a conditional transcript append boundary.
attempts.patch: Kept tests for final persistence and reopen, another tool and reuse, retention, preflight ordering, provider and invocation failures, append prefixes, transcript staleness, races, and exact call counts.

attempts.summary: Implemented one explicit durable continuation operation.
attempts.diagnostic: The runtime validates the original task/session/transcript and caller identities, calls the same provider once, then either records exact final content plus an Attempt or dispatches one tool and returns unchanged durable projections with a new continuation.
attempts.patch: Added continue_task_turn, typed stale-continuation handling, guarded session append support, broad integration coverage, and runtime/tool documentation.

attempts.summary: Fixed continuation races found by independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: A transcript could change while the provider was running: the initial implementation could dispatch a now-stale tool request or append final content after unrelated conversation progress.
attempts.patch: Added a post-provider transcript recheck before tool dispatch and an atomic expected-transcript guard for final assistant append, with RED race tests for both paths.

attempts.summary: Fixed metadata-only version retry behavior found by independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: A transcript projection can remain byte-equivalent while its stream version changes; retrying against only content could accept stale continuation ownership.
attempts.patch: Included authoritative session stream version in the continuation snapshot and stale check so metadata-only version movement invalidates the retry.

attempts.summary: Verified, obtained substantive exact-head review, and merged.
attempts.diagnostic: Pinned just verify and independent review passed after race fixes. GitHub Rust quality gate run 30138755979 succeeded. The initial CodeRabbit run was rate limited; after its cooldown, a deliberate exact-head review completed with only non-blocking nitpicks and zero review threads.
attempts.patch: Pull request 570 squash-merged as 5383171afe0809e3217327391332b1ae1054c9e1 and closed issue 569.

outcome.summary: Provider-tool continuations can now advance one explicit durable task turn at a time, rejecting stale or racing transcripts while retaining exact tool payloads only in memory.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test tool_task_runtime
Independent pre-commit review # transcript race and version findings fixed
GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30138755979 and substantive CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/570

lessons: Continuation ownership must include both transcript content and authoritative stream version so equivalent projections cannot hide intervening writes.
Validate again after an external provider call before dispatching a tool because preflight freshness can expire while control is outside the kernel.
Final transcript append needs an atomic expected-state guard; a separate recheck followed by append leaves a race window.
Explicit one-step progression keeps identity, authorization, failure prefixes, and retention visible at every provider/tool boundary.
A false-green rate-limited review must not race auto-merge; wait for cooldown and substantive exact-head review.
